page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, offering 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. The CPU instruction set features AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI vector extensions alongside AES encryption primitives.

System memory consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per vCPU). The instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for operating system and data volumes. Network throughput features a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. There are no discrete hardware accelerators bundled with this server type, leaving all computational workloads to the CPU cores.

Benchmark outcomes show modest throughput across standard synthetic evaluations. The server achieved a single-core score of 1103.19 and a multi-core score of 2934.5 in stress-ng tests. In Geekbench testing, it recorded 987.0 for single-core execution and 2173.0 for multi-core processing, with specific sub-scores including 2870.0 in Clang software compilation and 1915.0 in image processing. PassMark CPU testing yielded an overall score of 3628.64, while uncached memory bandwidth benchmarks registered 20.58 GB/sec read and 18.68 GB/sec write. Redis SET operations peaked at 2.86 million operations per second, accompanied by 3.36 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its compute-oriented core-to-memory balance and lack of bundled local disks, ecs.c5.xlarge represents a cost-conscious choice for modest utility workloads that do not require high memory density or extreme disk I/O. Appropriate deployments include small web servers, basic CI/CD runners, lightweight API endpoints, and low-scale batch data processing tasks.

The instance includes 0 GB of integrated local storage, requiring external block storage, and operates with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Across synthetic benchmarks, the instance delivers entry-level performance, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 2173.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3628.64. Redis throughput reaches 2.86 million operations per second, with web serving reaching 3.36 GB/sec. Without specialized GPU accelerators, ecs.c5.xlarge is best matched to entry-level compute tasks, small-scale web backends, CI/CD worker nodes, and basic utility services.
